{"memo": "Contents: Lists README topics: purpose, usage, install, use, API, examples, HTML, syntax, syntax tree, types, compatibility, related, contribute, license.

What is this? This package provides two extensions that add GFM table support to mdast for parsing and serializing. They plug into mdast-util-from-markdown for parsing tables and mdast-util-to-markdown for serializing tables.

When to use this: Use these extensions when working with mdast-util-from-markdown and mdast-util-to-markdown, combined with micromark-extension-gfm-table for parsing. For broader needs use micromark directly without trees or mdast-util-gfm for all GFM via remark-gfm, noting HTML conversion is handled by mdast-util-to-hast.

Install: This package is ESM only and requires Node 16 or newer for npm installation. It can also be imported in Deno and browsers using CDN URLs.

Use: The Use section demonstrates parsing an example markdown table into an mdast table tree and serializing it back with fromMarkdown and toMarkdown. It shows uneven input rows are normalized into aligned markdown output with positional info omitted.

API: The package exports gfmTableFromMarkdown to enable GFM tables in parsing and gfmTableToMarkdown with optional Options for serializing, with no default export. Options control tableCellPadding and tablePipeAlign plus a stringLength function for measuring cell width when aligning.

Examples: The Examples section shows how default alignment miscalculates visual width for full-width characters and emoji. It demonstrates fixing alignment by passing string-width as the stringLength option to gfmTableToMarkdown.

HTML: This utility does not handle conversion of markdown to HTML. That responsibility belongs to mdast-util-to-hast.

Syntax: The Syntax section defers to the syntax documentation in micromark-extension-gfm-table. It defines no additional syntax itself.

Syntax tree: This section defines Table, TableRow, and TableCell nodes added to mdast along with the alignType enumeration and updated flow, table, and row content models. It includes IDL definitions, field descriptions, alignment semantics, and a markdown to tree example.

Types: The package is fully typed with TypeScript and exports the additional Options type. The Table, TableRow, and TableCell node types are exposed from @types/mdast.

Compatibility: Projects are compatible with maintained Node versions, with the current major line targeting Node 16 after dropping unmaintained versions on major releases. It works with from-markdown version 2 or newer and to-markdown version 2 or newer.

Related: The Related section lists remark-gfm for GFM support in remark and mdast-util-gfm for all GFM extensions. It also references micromark-extension-gfm-table for low-level parsing of GFM tables.

Contribute: Contribution guidance points to the central contributing and support guides for getting started and getting help. It notes the project enforces a code of conduct for all interactions.

License: The project is licensed under MIT. Copyright is held by Titus Wormer.

Recommendation: For teams already using mdast-util-from-markdown and mdast-util-to-markdown that need GFM tables, adopt this focused, fully typed, MIT-licensed extension provided ESM on Node 16+ is acceptable; prefer mdast-util-gfm / remark-gfm for full GFM support or micromark for non-tree use, with HTML handled via mdast-util-to-hast.", "concerns": [], "rationale": "Assembled the one-page memo solely from Worker 1 Contents summary and Worker 2 per-section summaries in document order, one paragraph per section plus a closing recommendation, without extra file reads per assignment."}

{"memo": "Contents: Lists README sections: What is this, usage, install, API, examples, syntax, tree, types, compatibility, related, contribute, license.

What is this?: This package provides mdast extensions to parse and serialize GFM tables. They plug into mdast-util-from-markdown for parsing and mdast-util-to-markdown for serializing.

When to use this: Use this when you already work with mdast-util-from-markdown and mdast-util-to-markdown and need GFM table support, combining it with micromark-extension-gfm-table for parsing. For simpler cases use micromark directly without a tree, for full GFM use mdast-util-gfm or remark-gfm, while HTML conversion is handled by mdast-util-to-hast.

Install: This package is ESM only and requires Node 16 or newer with npm for installation. It can also be loaded in Deno and browsers through a CDN with bundle support for browsers.

Use: The guide shows reading an uneven markdown table into a table node with alignment data and text cells. Serializing back normalizes pipes and padding while filling missing cells to form a neat table.

API: This package exports two named identifiers and has no default export. One supports parsing tables from markdown and the other supports serializing tables back to markdown with optional settings.

gfmTableFromMarkdown: This function creates an mdast extension that enables GFM table parsing in mdast-util-from-markdown. It returns a FromMarkdownExtension for handling table syntax.

gfmTableToMarkdown(options?): This function creates an mdast extension that enables GFM table serialization in mdast-util-to-markdown. It accepts optional configuration and returns a ToMarkdownExtension for writing tables.

Options: Options configure padding between delimiters and cells, alignment of delimiters, and custom cell width measurement. Defaults enable padding and alignment and measure length by character count.

Examples: This section introduces practical formatting examples for the extensions. It currently contains a single detailed example focused on visual width and alignment.

Example: stringLength: This example shows misalignment when wide characters and emoji use simple character counts for pipe alignment. It then fixes alignment by passing a visual width function such as string-width to the serialization option.

HTML: This utility does not convert markdown to HTML by itself. That rendering step is delegated to mdast-util-to-hast.

Syntax: This section does not define table syntax itself. It refers readers to the syntax documentation in micromark-extension-gfm-table.

Syntax tree: This section defines the mdast interfaces added by this utility. It organizes them into nodes, enumerations, and content model rules.

Nodes: Nodes comprise Table for two dimensional data with optional column alignment, TableRow for rows, and TableCell for header or data cells. Tables live in flow content, rows live in tables, and cells hold phrasing content without breaks.

Enumeration: Enumeration defines alignType with left, right, center, and null values for column alignment. These mirror CSS text alignment semantics, with null deferring to host environment behavior.

Content model: The content model extends flow content to allow tables and restricts tables to rows and rows to cells. This enforces a strict table, row, and cell hierarchy for valid trees.

Types: This package is fully typed in TypeScript and exports the Options type. Table node types are available separately from the mdast type definitions.

Compatibility: Projects from the unified collective track maintained Node versions and currently support Node 16 for this line. It requires mdast-util-from-markdown version 2 or newer and mdast-util-to-markdown version 2 or newer.

Related: This section lists related GFM tooling including remark-gfm, mdast-util-gfm, and the micromark table extension. These cover broader GFM support or lower level parsing for different use cases.

Contribute: This section points to contribution and support guides in the shared community health repository. It also notes that a code of conduct governs interaction with the project.

License: This package is released under the MIT license. Copyright is held by Titus Wormer.

Recommendation: For teams already on the mdast-util-from-markdown / to-markdown stack needing standard GFM tables, adopt mdast-util-gfm-table for its focused parsing/serialization, ESM TypeScript support, and clear upgrade path to mdast-util-gfm/remark-gfm if full GFM is later required.", "concerns": [], "rationale": "Assembled memo solely from Worker 1 Contents summary and Worker 2 section summaries in document order, one paragraph per section plus closing recommendation, without reading source file or adding external facts."}

{"memo": "Contents: Contents lists all README topics: purpose, usage, install, use, API, examples, HTML, syntax, syntax tree, types, compatibility, related, contribute, license.

What is this?: This package provides two mdast extensions that add support for GFM table syntax to mdast. They plug into mdast-util-from-markdown for parsing tables into syntax trees and mdast-util-to-markdown for serializing trees back to markdown.

When to use this: Use these extensions when already working with mdast-util-from-markdown and mdast-util-to-markdown, combined with micromark-extension-gfm-table for parsing. If you don't need a syntax tree use micromark directly, if you want all of GFM use mdast-util-gfm or remark-gfm, and for HTML conversion use mdast-util-to-hast as this utility does not handle it.

Install: This package is ESM-only and requires Node.js 16 or newer when installed via npm as `npm install mdast-util-gfm-table`. It can also be imported in Deno and browsers via esm.sh URLs with optional bundling for browsers.

Use: The Use section demonstrates parsing an example markdown table with uneven rows and alignment markers into a `table` node via `fromMarkdown` with `gfmTable()` and `gfmTableFromMarkdown()`. It then shows serializing the tree back to normalized, pipe-aligned markdown with `toMarkdown` and `gfmTableToMarkdown()` including alignment metadata.

API: This package exports the identifiers `gfmTableFromMarkdown` and `gfmTableToMarkdown` with no default export. The following subsections detail their signatures, parameters, return values, and configuration options.

gfmTableFromMarkdown: This function creates a FromMarkdownExtension for mdast-util-from-markdown to enable GFM table parsing. It takes no options and returns the extension object used in parsing.

gfmTableToMarkdown(options?): This function creates a ToMarkdownExtension for mdast-util-to-markdown to enable GFM table serialization. It accepts an optional Options object for configuration and returns the corresponding serialization extension.

Options: Options is the TypeScript configuration type for serialization. It defines `tableCellPadding` and `tablePipeAlign` booleans defaulting to true, plus a `stringLength` function defaulting to `s => s.length` for measuring cell content width when aligning delimiters.

Examples: This section introduces practical examples for configuring the extensions. It currently contains a single detailed example on custom `stringLength` handling.

Example: stringLength: This example shows how default alignment miscalculates visual width for full-width characters like Chinese and emoji, and how to fix it. It demonstrates passing `string-width` as the `stringLength` option to `gfmTableToMarkdown()` to produce correctly aligned tables.

HTML: This utility does not convert markdown to HTML. That rendering step is handled separately by mdast-util-to-hast.

Syntax: The Syntax section defers to the syntax documentation in micromark-extension-gfm-table. It defines no additional syntax itself and serves as a cross-reference.

Syntax tree: This section specifies the mdast interfaces added by the utility. It is organized into Nodes, Enumeration, and Content model subsections that define structure, alignment values, and hierarchy.

Nodes: The Nodes subsection defines `Table`, `TableRow`, and `TableCell` interfaces with their types, parent relationships, allowed content, and alignment semantics. It includes markdown-to-tree examples illustrating headers, alignment arrays, and phrasing-only cell content excluding Break nodes.

{"memo": "Executive Summary — mdast-util-gfm-table — Library Selection Memo for Architecture Council

Contents: The README opens with a Contents listing all major topics — purpose, usage, install, API, examples, HTML, syntax, tree, types, compatibility, related, contribute, and license — providing a map for the detailed guidance that follows.

What is this?: This package provides two extensions that add GFM table support to mdast. They plug into parsing and serialization utilities to convert between markdown tables and syntax trees.

When to use this: Use these extensions when you already work with the mdast parsing and serialization utilities and need table support combined with the micromark table extension. If you need no syntax tree or want all GFM features or easier transforms or HTML output, use micromark directly or the full GFM utilities or remark GFM or the hast converter instead.

Install: This package is ESM only and is installed with npm for Node version 16 and newer. It can also be loaded in Deno and browsers through a CDN with module and bundle options.

Use: The Use section walks through parsing a sample markdown table into a syntax tree and serializing it back to normalized markdown. It shows the required wiring of the micromark table extension with the fromMarkdown and toMarkdown functions.

API: The package exports two factory functions for parsing and serializing tables with no default export and an optional configuration object for serialization. The configuration controls cell padding and pipe alignment and custom measurement of cell content width for alignment.

Examples: The Examples section demonstrates fixing visual misalignment of wide characters and emoji by supplying a custom width function. It compares default alignment with improved alignment achieved by using an external visual width package.

HTML: This utility does not handle conversion from markdown to HTML. That responsibility is delegated to a separate hast conversion utility.

Syntax: The Syntax section defers to the micromark table extension documentation for the full syntax definition. It provides no additional syntax details itself.

Syntax tree: The Syntax tree section defines Table and TableRow and TableCell nodes with alignment data and allowed content models for mdast. It includes the alignment enumeration and flow and table and row content rules with a markdown to tree example.

Types: The package is fully typed in TypeScript and exports the additional Options type. The table node types are exposed from the external mdast type definitions.

Compatibility: Projects maintained by the unified collective stay compatible with maintained versions of Node with the current major line targeting Node version 16. This utility requires version 2 or later of both the fromMarkdown and toMarkdown utilities.

Related: The Related section lists companion packages for remark GFM support and full GFM utilities and micromark table parsing. It situates this focused table package within the wider unified ecosystem.

Contribute: Contribution guidance points to the shared contributing guide for ways to get started and the support guide for ways to get help. It notes that a code of conduct governs interaction with the repository and community.

License: The project is released under the MIT license. Copyright is held by Titus Wormer.

Recommendation: For mdast-based markdown pipelines requiring GFM tables, adopt mdast-util-gfm-table wired with micromark table extensions and mdast-util-from/to-markdown; for full GFM, remark-level authoring, or direct HTML, prefer mdast-util-gfm, remark-gfm, or mdast-util-to-hast instead. {"memo": "Contents: The README opens with a Contents table listing all sections — intro, usage, install, API, examples, syntax, tree, types, compatibility, related, contribute, and license — to orient readers.

What is this?: This package provides two mdast extensions that add GFM table support to markdown parsing and serialization. They plug into mdast-util-from-markdown to parse tables into syntax trees and mdast-util-to-markdown to serialize trees back to markdown.

When to use this: Use this when you already work with mdast-util-from-markdown and mdast-util-to-markdown and need GFM tables, pairing the parser side with micromark-extension-gfm-table. For no syntax tree use micromark directly, for all of GFM use mdast-util-gfm, for easier transforms use remark-gfm, and for HTML output use mdast-util-to-hast since this package does not handle HTML.

Install: This package is ESM only and requires Node version 16 or newer when used with npm installation. It can also be loaded in Deno and browsers through a CDN using module imports with pinned versions.

Use: Import the micromark table extension alongside fromMarkdown with gfmTableFromMarkdown to parse a markdown table into a table node with aligned rows and cells. Then pass the resulting tree to toMarkdown with gfmTableToMarkdown to serialize it back to normalized markdown with aligned delimiters.

API: The package exports two named identifiers for markdown parsing and serialization with no default export. The parsing helper takes no options while the serialization helper accepts an optional configuration object described in the Options section.

gfmTableFromMarkdown: It creates a from-markdown extension that enables GFM table parsing in mdast-util-from-markdown. It returns a FromMarkdownExtension object that integrates table token handling into the syntax tree builder.

gfmTableToMarkdown(options?): It creates a to-markdown extension that enables GFM table serialization in mdast-util-to-markdown. It accepts an optional Options object for formatting and returns a ToMarkdownExtension for use in serialization.

Options: It defines TypeScript configuration with tableCellPadding to control spacing around cell content and tablePipeAlign to control delimiter alignment. It also provides stringLength to measure cell content width for alignment with a default based on string length.

Examples: This section introduces practical formatting cases that show how serialization options affect rendered markdown tables. It currently contains a focused demonstration of custom cell width measurement for improved visual alignment.

Example: stringLength: It demonstrates how default alignment miscalculates visual width for full width characters and emoji in table cells. It then shows passing a visual width function such as string-width as stringLength to produce correctly aligned output.

HTML: This utility does not convert markdown to HTML on its own. That responsibility belongs to mdast-util-to-hast which transforms the syntax tree into HTML nodes.

Syntax: The allowed table syntax is not defined here in detail. Readers are referred to the Syntax section of micromark-extension-gfm-table for the full specification.

Syntax tree: This section defines the additional mdast interfaces introduced by the utility for representing tables. It covers node types plus alignment enumeration and content model rules for valid nesting.

Nodes: It groups the three new node types that model tables in the syntax tree. Each node entry details its type name plus allowed parents and children with illustrative structure.

Table: Table represents two dimensional data as flow content whose children must be table rows with the first row serving as column labels. It carries an optional align list of left right center or null values that controls column alignment as shown in the markdown example.

TableRow: TableRow represents a single row of cells within a table and belongs in table content. Its children must be table cells and a head row defines the column labels for its parent table.

TableCell: TableCell represents a header cell when in a head row or a data cell otherwise and belongs in row content. Its content model is phrasing content excluding Break nodes as illustrated by the parent table example.

Enumeration: It defines shared enumerations used by the table nodes. It currently documents only the alignment type with its allowed values and semantics.

alignType: AlignType describes horizontal alignment of phrasing content following CSS text alignment concepts. Allowed values are left right and center mapping to CSS meanings plus null for host defined alignment.

Content model: It specifies how the new table constructs integrate into existing mdast content categories. It defines extended flow content plus strict table content and row content types for rows and cells.

FlowContent (GFM table): It extends standard flow content to also permit Table nodes wherever flow is expected. This change allows tables to appear alongside paragraphs and other block level structures.

TableContent: It restricts table children to only TableRow nodes representing rows. This rule ensures a consistent two dimensional structure without stray content inside tables.

RowContent: It restricts row children to only TableCell nodes representing cells. This rule ensures rows contain only cells that in turn hold phrasing content.

Types: The package is fully typed in TypeScript and exposes its Options type for consumers. The Table TableRow and TableCell node types themselves are provided through the shared mdast type definitions.

Compatibility: Maintained unified projects track maintained Node versions with the current line supporting Node 16 and newer after major releases drop older runtimes. This release line works with version 2 and newer of both mdast-util-from-markdown and mdast-util-to-markdown.

Related: It lists companion projects for broader or lower level GFM table handling. Linked entries include remark-gfm for remark users plus mdast-util-gfm for full GFM support and the micromark table extension for parsing.

Contribute: It points to shared contributing and support guides for getting started and getting help. It also notes that interaction is governed by the project code of conduct.

License: The project is released under the MIT license. Copyright is held by Titus Wormer as noted in the license file.

Recommendation: For the council, recommend approval for any mdast-based pipeline that requires GFM tables, using this package together with micromark-extension-gfm-table and mdast-util-to-hast for HTML, with attention to ESM-only Node 16+ requirements and stringLength tuning for wide-character alignment; otherwise prefer mdast-util-gfm or remark-gfm for full GFM coverage.",

When should I use this? This package is useful when you are making your own micromark extensions. It should be used when you need standard label parsing in custom syntax.

Install: This package is ESM only and requires Node 16 or newer for npm installation. It can also be imported in Deno and browsers via esm.sh.

Use: Shows importing factoryLabel and using it inside a custom micromark tokenizer to parse definition labels.

API: This module exports only the identifier factoryLabel with no default export. It provides the low-level interface for custom tokenizers to invoke label parsing.

factoryLabel(…): The factoryLabel function parses labels capped at 999 characters in the string, handling examples like [a] and escaped variants. It takes tokenize context, effects, ok and nok states, and whole, marker and string types, and returns a start state.

Types: This package is fully typed with TypeScript. It exports no additional types.

Compatibility: Maintained projects stay compatible with maintained Node versions, with the current 2.x line targeting Node 16. This package works with micromark 3.

Security: This package is described as safe. Security reports should follow the process in security.md in micromark/.github.

Contribute: Contribution guidance is in contributing.md and help is in support.md in micromark/.github. This project enforces a code of conduct that all participants must follow.

License: This project is licensed under MIT. Copyright is held by Titus Wormer.

{"memo":"Contents: This part lists all topics and links to guide navigation of the document. It outlines the order from introduction through install and use to API, types, compatibility, security, contribute and license.

What is this?: This package provides a micromark factory for parsing markdown labels found in media and definitions. It exposes reusable tokenizer states for extension authors.

When should I use this?: Use this package when building custom micromark extensions that need label parsing. It is intended for extension developers rather than general markdown users.

Install: This package is ESM only and installs with npm for Node 16 and newer. It also loads in Deno and browsers through a CDN with a bundled option for browsers.

Use: Shows importing factoryLabel and using it inside a micromark tokenizer to parse definition labels.

API: This module exports only the identifier factoryLabel with no default export. Full behavior and arguments are detailed in its factoryLabel subsection.

factoryLabel(…): It parses labels capped at 999 characters in the string, and takes context, effects, success and failure states, plus types for the whole label, markers, and string, to return the start state. It supports single line, multiline, and escaped bracket labels as shown in the examples.

Types: This package is fully typed with TypeScript for type safety. It exports no additional types.

Compatibility: Unified collective projects stay compatible with maintained Node versions, with the current line supporting Node 16 and micromark 3. Support for unmaintained Node versions is dropped at each new major release.

Security: This package is considered safe with no special handling required. Reports should follow the process in the security document in the micromark GitHub organization.

Contribute: Getting started guidance is in the contributing document and help options are in the support document in the micromark GitHub organization. Contributors must follow the code of conduct when interacting with the community.

License: This project uses the MIT license with copyright held by Titus Wormer. Reuse is permitted under the MIT terms.

Recommendation: For teams building custom micromark extensions that need standard-compliant label parsing, this focused, typed, MIT-licensed factory is a low-risk reuse candidate provided the ESM-only Node 16+ and micromark 3 stack is acceptable; general markdown users should rely on higher-level extensions rather than adopting it directly.","concerns":[],"rationale":"Assembled memo in document order from W1 Use summary and W2 summaries for all other sections, one paragraph per section plus closing recommendation, without reading file directly per orchestrator split."}

{"memo": "Executive Summary — micromark-factory-label

Contents: The Contents section provides linked navigation to all main sections and the factoryLabel API subsection. It contains no substantive documentation beyond the table of contents itself.

What is this?: This package exposes tokenizer states to parse labels found in media and definitions. It is a low-level micromark factory rather than a standalone markdown feature.

When should I use this?: This package is useful when building custom micromark extensions that need label parsing. It is not intended for end users parsing markdown directly.

Install: The package is ESM only and is installed with npm on Node.js version 16 or newer. It can also be imported in Deno and browsers via esm.sh URLs.

Use: Example imports factoryLabel and demonstrates custom definition tokenizer calling factoryLabel with effects, markers, and string types.

API: The module exports a single named identifier factoryLabel with no default export. This section introduces its purpose and signature details.

factoryLabel: It parses labels such as [a] with string content capped at 999 characters and takes tokenize context, effects, ok and nok states, plus types for the whole label, markers, and string. It returns the start state for the tokenizer.

Types: The package is fully typed with TypeScript. It exports no additional custom types.

Compatibility: Projects in the unified collective support maintained versions of Node.js and drop unmaintained versions on new major releases. The current line targets Node.js 16 compatibility and works with micromark version 3.

Security: The package is described as safe. Security reports should be submitted following security.md in the micromark dot-github repository.

Contribute: Contribution guidance is found in contributing.md and help options in support.md within micromark dot-github. The project enforces a code of conduct for all interaction.

License: The project is licensed under MIT. Copyright belongs to Titus Wormer.
